<Rep. Jared Huffman>: The critical minerals and critical materials lists provide important strategic direction for decision-makers to prioritize government actions and investments to secure vulnerable mineral and materials supply chains.
While Natural Resources Committee Democrats support H.R. 755, these lists are only useful if they are unbiased. The Energy Act of 2020 dictated a deliberative, science-based process for creating the critical minerals list, mandating transparent methodologies and opportunities for stakeholder input.
The Trump administration has blatantly violated the letter and spirit of the Energy Act of 2020 by including metallurgical coal and uranium in the final 2025 United States Geological Survey (USGS) critical minerals list at the direction of the President. The Energy Act of 2020 specifically prohibits the inclusion of ``fuel minerals'' on the list. USGS failed to provide the Natural Resources Committee minority with the requested information on the legal justification and any data and analyses shared with USGS by the Department of Energy as justification for these inclusions.
Political interference with this process erodes the lists' reliability as a decision-making tool. These actions undermine the United States' economic and national security by compromising efforts to target federal investments and interventions towards the most important, at-risk mineral and materials supply chains.
Jared Huffman,
Ranking Member.
